subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: What public scheduler/config contract should OpenClaw use for foreground per-agent command lane isolation on shared gateways?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and scheduler semantics that must settle lane ownership, aggregate caps, and trust boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Trusted Per-Agent Foreground Lanes
options.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned foreground lanes while retaining a separate global safety cap.

options.title: Unified Scheduler Design First
options.body: Defer this issue until foreground, subagent, hook, and workload-specific lanes can share one coordinated scheduler contract.

options.title: Document Process Isolation Only
options.body: Keep the shared `main` lane as the product model and document separate gateway processes for heavy-agent isolation.

recommendation.title: Trusted Per-Agent Foreground Lanes
recommendation.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned foreground lanes while retaining a separate global safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal runs through the command queue, command-lane enum, and agent concurrency resolver work authored by steipete.
